analysis.title: Global Weekly Kickstart: Rising Yields Challenge Earnings Strength
key_insights: Global equities fell 0.7% last week. Europe fell 2.2% and the US fell 0.3%. Technology (+1.4%) was the only sector with a meaningful gain, and Financials fell 3.0%.
European equity resilience is earnings-led. Year-to-date EPS revisions explain almost 70% of relative sector moves. Consensus expects 22% y/y EPS growth in 2H, or 15% excluding Energy.
Market breadth is close to normal. Europe's median stock is outperforming its US and Asian counterparts.

Higher yields and sovereign spreads increasingly constrain European valuations. Each 10bp rise in German Bund yields corresponds to roughly a 1.2% fall in the STOXX 600. A 10bp widening in average OAT and BTP spreads to Bunds takes 0.9% off Europe's P/E.
GS favours durable earnings alongside shareholder returns. Europe offers a 5.5% FCF yield versus 3.5% in the US. Buybacks and limited issuance keep equity supply negative.
GS remains overweight Technology, Banks, Renewables, Defense and Capital intensive in Europe.
Rising global bond yields weighed on Gold, which fell 3.2% on the week. Germany's 10-year government bonds returned 1.4%, which GS reads as safe-haven demand.
Brazilian equities rose 4.7% on growing expectations of a potential Bolsonaro victory.
Europe's weekly sector moves were large. European banks fell sharply (Germany -8.2%, France -8.6% in the sector table). European semiconductors rose (Germany +12.8%, France +10.4%).
GS 12-month targets imply upside of 12.7% for the S&P 500 (7723 to 8700), 10.1% for the STOXX 600 (631 to 695), 12.4% for Topix (4091 to 4600) and 27.3% for MSCI Asia-Pacific ex-Japan (880 to 1120).
GS forecasts the US 10-year yield falling from 5.3% to 4.7% in 3 months, 4.6% in 6 months and 4.4% in 12 months, a 83bp decline to the 12-month point. German 10-year yields go from 3.4% to 3.3%.
GS forecasts Brent falling from $102.3/bbl to $84 in 3 months and $77 in 12 months, and Gold rising from $4145/oz to $5235 in 12 months (+26.3%).
Consensus 2026 EPS growth is 31.8% for the S&P 500, 19.3% for the STOXX 600 and 34.3% for MSCI AC World. IT is 86.1% in 2026 and 41.2% in 2027. Energy is 78.4% in 2026 and -11.3% in 2027.
The GS Bull/Bear Market Indicator is at the 67th percentile. The Shiller PE of 40.9 is at the 98th percentile.
On 12-month forward P/E, the US is at 19.4 versus 16.3 for AC World, 15.8 for Japan and 13.7 for Europe. Growth sectors are at 20.6 against 12.0 for Financials.

GS sector weights: Europe is overweight Financials, IT and Communication services, and underweight Consumer discretionary and Health care. The US is overweight Materials and Health care. Japan and Asia-Pacific ex-Japan are overweight Industrials, Financials and IT.
This week's macro calendar includes the US trade balance and September FOMC minutes, European September PMIs and August industrial production, the BOJ branch managers' meeting and the RBI meeting.
